subject: Discovery: Observability & Evals — Recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@zenhealth.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: Observability & Evals — Recap and next steps

Hi Jordan / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really helpful conversation diving into where ZenHealth is on model observability and evals. Below is a short recap, what success looks like for you, and proposed next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

One-line summary
- Primary goal: get predictable, production-grade observability for LLM outputs + an evals workflow that catches regressions before rollouts.

Pain points you shared
- Lack of per-route visibility: product teams can’t see token-level cost or per-prompt latency, making it hard to attribute cost to features.
- Silent quality regressions: changes to models/quantization have introduced subtle prompt regressions that are discovered too late.
- Rollout risk: no easy guardrails for canary rollouts tied to golden prompt sets / regression alerts.
- Tracing gaps: limited request tracing across service boundaries (user request -> model call -> downstream scoring), making root cause analysis slow.

Current stack highlights
- Core model hosting: in-house endpoints on GCP (K8s + TPU/GPU), using a bespoke inference layer.
- Logging: ELK stack for infra logs; minimal structured telemetry for prompts/outputs.
- CI/evals: ad-hoc eval scripts run pre-release; no central golden prompt sets or automated regression alerts.

Success criteria (what we heard)
- Dashboards showing per-route token cost, p50/p95 latency, and user-facing metric impact (CSAT/drop rate)
- Tracing hooks that link a user request to model prompts + downstream scoring services
- Golden prompt sets per product area with automated regression detection and alerting (daily runs + immediate alerts on significant delta)
- Rollout guardrails: automatic rollback / traffic split adjustments when regression thresholds are exceeded during canary

Specific observability / evals asks you requested
- Per-route/model dashboards (cost, latency, quality trends) — want starter dashboards for Clinical Summaries and Intake Triage flows.
- Tracing hooks / header propagation guidance — examples for instrumenting front-end -> API -> model call.
- Golden prompt sets & evaluation harness recommendation — sample CSV/JSON format and run schedule.
- Regression alerting policies + suggested thresholds and incident playbook.
- Deployment guardrails: canary config suggestions and automatic fallback policies.

Attachments
- Attached: zenhealth-observability-asks.pdf (one-pager recap of the above + starter dashboard mockups).

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive demo: 45–60 min with engineering (we recommend including your infra lead and someone from product). Dylan (SE) will lead a walkthrough of tracing hooks and dashboard instrumentation.
2) Share golden prompt set template and an eval run example (we’ll send sample files).
3) Draft mutual action plan (MAP) for pilot focusing on 2 product routes (Clinical Summaries + Intake Triage).

Proposed timing
- Demo: this week or early next week — suggested slots: Thu 11th 10:00–11:00 PT or Mon 15th 09:00–10:00 PT.
- MAP + sample artifacts: by EOD Friday.

Thanks — excited to move forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the conversation. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

- Data residency: for the pilot we need to confirm where logs/telemetry will be stored. We prefer US-only retention in our GCP project.
- SSO / RBAC: can you include expected role mappings for dev, prod, and auditors in the MAP?
- Volume: Clinical Summaries currently ~120k tokens/day; Intake Triage ~30k tokens/day. Helpful for sizing.

We can do the demo Thu 11th at 10:00 PT — Jordan (me) + Priya (product) + our infra lead (Raj) will join.

Also: please include a short sample of the golden prompt CSV and an example of the regression alert email we’d receive so we can share with our incident response folks.

On attachments: I see the PDF — thanks. Could you also add the MAP as an editable spreadsheet so we can comment inline?

Best,
Jordan
Senior Product Manager
ZenHealth
